subprocess_flow.description: The Inventory Planner initiates the automated diagnostic tool to extract replenishment data, supplier lead time history, and shrinkage reports from the ERP and Warehouse Management Systems. This step ensures that all quantitative data points required for a factual analysis are gathered and consolidated into a single working environment.
subprocess_flow.end_conditions: All required data sets are successfully extracted and consolidated.
triggers: Replenishment order initiation following a stock-out crisis.
subprocess_flow.scope: Extraction and consolidation of historical inventory and supply chain data.
subprocess_flow.purpose: To provide a factual foundation for the root cause investigation.
subprocess_flow.governance_requirements: Data privacy and system access audit logs.
success_criteria: Dataset contains all 3 required input types.

subprocess_flow.end_conditions: Correlation patterns are identified and quantified.

step_risks_and_controls.control: Planner review of automated correlation findings.

subprocess_flow.purpose: To isolate external supply and demand factors contributing to the stock-out.
subprocess_flow.scope: Analytical correlation of external market and supplier data.
subprocess_flow.description: The Inventory Planner utilizes the diagnostic tools to perform a correlation analysis between sales spikes and supplier delivery delays. By mapping these two variables, the planner can determine if the stock-out was primarily caused by an unexpected surge in demand, a failure in the supply chain timeline, or a combination of both.
success_criteria: Primary external driver (Supply vs Demand) identified.

subprocess_flow.description: The Inventory Planner investigates internal records to identify operational issues such as inventory shrinkage, data entry errors, or warehouse delays. This step ensures that internal inefficiencies are not overlooked when assigning responsibility for the stock-out event.
subprocess_flow.purpose: To identify internal process failures that contributed to inventory depletion.
subprocess_flow.scope: Review of internal warehouse and inventory management operations.
triggers: Availability of shrinkage and warehouse data.

step_risks_and_controls.control: Cross-referencing shrinkage reports with physical cycle counts.

triggers: Completion of correlation and internal analyses.
subprocess_flow.end_conditions: Initial draft of the RCA report is completed.
subprocess_flow.scope: Drafting of the formal analysis document.
subprocess_flow.substep_name: Generate Draft Root Cause Analysis Report
success_criteria: Draft report covers both external and internal factors.
subprocess_flow.purpose: To synthesize data into a cohesive explanation of the stock-out.

step_risks_and_controls.risk: Over-reliance on automated report generation without context.

subprocess_flow.description: The Inventory Planner generates the initial draft of the Root Cause Analysis (RCA) report, combining the automated correlation results with the internal factor analysis. The planner adds qualitative context to the pre-populated data to provide a comprehensive narrative of the event.

dependencies: Generate Draft Root Cause Analysis Report
success_criteria: Root cause clearly identified for the event.
subprocess_flow.purpose: To ensure the analysis is accurate before being used for strategic decision-making.
subprocess_flow.description: The Inventory Planner reviews the draft report for accuracy, completeness, and clarity. Final adjustments are made to the narrative to ensure it meets the success criteria of identifying a clear root cause, preparing it for management review and database entry.
triggers: Completion of the draft RCA report.
subprocess_flow.governance_requirements: Quality assurance review by the Inventory Planner.
subprocess_flow.scope: Final review and polishing of the RCA document.
subprocess_flow.end_conditions: Final RCA report is ready for distribution and filing.

subprocess_flow.governance_requirements: Adherence to inventory optimization mathematical models.
subprocess_flow.description: Based on the findings in the RCA report, the Inventory Planner calculates new safety stock levels, reorder points, and lead time assumptions. These recommendations are designed to adjust the system parameters to prevent a recurrence of the stock-out under similar conditions.
subprocess_flow.purpose: To translate analysis into actionable preventative measures.
subprocess_flow.end_conditions: Specific parameter adjustment recommendations are formulated.
success_criteria: Recommendations address the identified root cause.

subprocess_flow.scope: Data entry into the centralized tracking system.
subprocess_flow.end_conditions: The database record is saved and verified.
subprocess_flow.governance_requirements: Data integrity and audit trail requirements.
success_criteria: Record is searchable and correctly categorized.

step_risks_and_controls.control: Database validation rules for mandatory fields.

subprocess_flow.description: The Inventory Planner enters the final root cause findings and the summary of the event into the organization's centralized root cause database. This ensures that historical data is available for trend analysis and long-term strategic planning.
subprocess_flow.purpose: To maintain a historical record of supply chain failures for continuous improvement.

subprocess_flow.description: The Inventory Planner submits the Final RCA Report and the Safety Stock Adjustment Recommendations to the Inventory Control Manager. The Manager reviews the documents and provides formal sign-off, authorizing the implementation of the recommended parameter changes.
subprocess_flow.scope: Review and approval of proposed inventory changes.
subprocess_flow.governance_requirements: Monthly sign-off by Inventory Control Manager.
triggers: Submission of recommendations and RCA report.
success_criteria: Formal sign-off obtained for 100% of validated recommendations.
subprocess_flow.purpose: To ensure managerial oversight and accountability for inventory strategy changes.
subprocess_flow.end_conditions: Managerial approval is received and documented.
